C0.quote: extensive research on the design of voting systems for participatory budgeting
C0.note: Approximate proportional core for participatory budgeting and committee selection (voting on outcomes from voters' preferences).

C1.loc: 4. Main Result, Theorem 4.1, p.7; 5. Committee Selection, Theorem 5.1, p.10
C1.quote: under Assumption 1, there exists a 6.24-approximate core solution.
C1.note: Main results are existence of outcomes in the gamma-approximate (proportional) core, a fairness property; the approximation factor relaxes a property rather than approximating an optimum of a welfare objective, so WD is not coded. Algorithms are constructive proof devices and the conclusion puts computational aspects beyond scope, so AL is not coded.

C2.1.loc: 2. Notations and Preliminaries, p.3; 5. Committee Selection, p.10

C2.2.loc: 2. Notations and Preliminaries, p.3; 5. Committee Selection, Def. 5.1-5.2 and Sec. 5.1, p.10
C2.2.quote: Note that both ranking and approval preferences may allow ties.
C2.2.note: General model: strict preference orders over outcomes ('We assume that the order is strict'). Section 5: ranking preferences induced by an item ranking and approval preferences given by an approved set Mi; the induced preferences over committees may have ties (weak orders). No input format outside the listed codes, so OTH is not needed.

C2.3.quote: voters have ordinal preferences over combinations of projects
C2.3.note: Voters are attributed preferences (and, for approval preferences, utilities u_i(S)).

C2.4.quote: preference order ⪰i over O. We assume that the order is strict.
C2.4.note: The rule's argument is the agents' preference orders, applied directly; the abstract says participants 'submit ordinal preferences' but only to contrast the format with numerical utilities, not to state that submitted equals held preferences.

C1.reason: The gamma-approximate core is a relaxed proportionality property, not performance against a welfare/distortion objective, so the results are axiomatic (AX) only.

C2.2.reason: The general model uses strict orders (RANK), Section 5 uses approval sets (APPR) and explicitly allows ties in the induced committee preferences (WEAK), while B's OTH describes strict orders already covered by RANK.

C6.VOT.reason: C6 counts types whose actions are fixed by the model, and voters supplying their exogenous preferences to the rule is such a fixed (non-strategic, implicitly sincere) action, consistent with C3.1 = NONE.
